Read docs/TASK_P6_git.md section 2.2 (the type block, runGit and gitOk) and section 4. Write two files. src/git/types.ts: exactly the types of the section 2.2 block, no values, importing Deck from "../cards/types.js" with `import type`. src/git/run.ts: `export function runGit(root, args, env): GitResult` and `export function gitOk(root, args, env): string`, importing spawnSync from "node:child_process" (this is the only file of src/git that may import it) and the GitResult type from "./types.js". runGit calls spawnSync("git", args, {cwd: root, env: {...env, LC_ALL: "C", GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: "0"}, encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 67108864}); the child gets exactly that env: never read or spread the process environment. A spawn error gives {code: null, stdout: "", stderr: "git could not start: " + error.message}; runGit never throws. gitOk returns stdout untouched when code is 0, else throws new Error("git " + args[0] + " failed (exit " + String(code) + "): " + the first line of stderr.trim()). Write no test file: a probe tests you and the judge writes the example tests.

## Function Run Git

One synchronous git call with an explicit environment; the only spawner of the Component.

Behaviour: runGit(root, args, env) spawns `git` with args, cwd = root, env = the given env with LC_ALL=C and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 laid over it (nothing of the parent process is inherited), synchronously, stdout and stderr captured as UTF-8 text. Returns Git Result {code: the exit status (null when killed or not started), stdout, stderr}; a spawn failure gives code null and stderr "git could not start: <message>". It never throws. gitOk(root, args, env) runs runGit and returns stdout when code is 0; otherwise it throws Error("git <args[0]> failed (exit <code>): <first line of the trimmed stderr>").

Steps:
- produces: Git Result

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given a fresh repo (tmpRepo, branch main); env {PATH, HOME: the repo root, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: "1", GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: "Ada", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: "ada@example.invalid", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME: "Ada", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL: "ada@example.invalid"}; args ["rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"]; when runGit; then {code: 0, stdout: "main\n", stderr: ""}
2. given the same repo and env plus FOO "bar" and LC_ALL "de_DE.UTF-8"; args ["-c", "alias.envs=!echo \"$LC_ALL $GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT $FOO ${USER-unset}\"", "envs"]; when runGit; then {code: 0, stdout: "C 0 bar unset\n", stderr: ""} — LC_ALL and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT forced, the given env passed, nothing of the parent environment (USER) leaks
3. given the same repo and env; args ["checkout", "nope"]; when runGit, then gitOk; then runGit gives code 1, stdout "", stderr beginning "error: pathspec 'nope' did not match"; gitOk throws an Error whose message begins "git checkout failed (exit 1): error: pathspec 'nope' did not match"

Data Git Result: What one git call returned.
Schema:
{ code: number | null, stdout: string, stderr: string }

Module: `src/git/types.ts`; test: `src/git/run.ts`.

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response and Stub Answer are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation (P4). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

Write the files: `src/git/types.ts`, `src/git/run.ts`.

Read docs/TASK_P6_git.md section 2.2 (commitPaths, commitCard, makeCommitHook) and section 4. Write one file src/git/commit.ts exporting three functions, importing gitOk from "./run.js" and the types CardCommit, CardCommitter, CommitInfo, Trailer from "./types.js" (`import type`). Do not import src/runloop: CommitInfo and CardCommitter are structurally runloop's CommitInfo and CommitHook (src/runloop/types.ts is in your context only to show that shape). commitPaths(root, paths, subject, trailers, env): gitOk add -A -- paths; gitOk diff --cached --name-only -- paths, empty after trim → return null; else gitOk(["commit", "-q", "-m", subject, "-m", trailer lines "<key>: <value>" joined by "\n", "--", ...paths]) (no --no-verify), commit = rev-parse HEAD trimmed, the diffstat from `git show --numstat --format= <commit>` per section 2.2 ("-" counts 0). commitCard builds the subject "morph <customId>: <targets joined by ', '>" and the trailers Morph-Card, Morph-Model, Morph-Variant only when variant !== null, Morph-Acceptance-Exit (String of the number), in that order, and calls commitPaths over input.targets. makeCommitHook(root, model, env) returns (customId, targets) => commitCard(root, {customId, targets, model, variant: null, acceptanceExit: 0}, env). Write no test file.

## Function Commit Paths

Stages exactly the given paths and commits them with a subject and trailers; null when nothing changed.

Behaviour: commitPaths(root, paths, subject, trailers, env): `git add -A -- <paths>`; `git diff --cached --name-only -- <paths>` empty → null, no commit. Else `git commit -q -m <subject> -m <trailer block> -- <paths>`, the trailer block being one "<key>: <value>" line per trailer in the given order joined by "\n" (hooks run; nothing is bypassed), so the message is "<subject>\n\n<trailer lines>". Only the paths are committed: a file staged by hand or modified outside them stays as it was. Then commit = `git rev-parse HEAD` (trimmed) and the diffstat from `git show --numstat --format= <commit>`: files = the number of non-empty lines, insertions and deletions the sums of the first two columns ("-" for a binary file counts 0). Returns Commit Info.

Steps:
- calls: Run Git
- produces: Commit Info

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given a fresh repo; other.txt written and staged by hand (git add other.txt); notes.txt untracked; src/a.ts written "export const a = 1;\n"; paths ["src/a.ts"], subject "s", trailers [["K", "v"]]; when committed; then Commit Info {commit: HEAD (40 hex), diffstat {files: 1, insertions: 1, deletions: 0}}; the HEAD message is "s\n\nK: v"; `git show --name-only --format= HEAD` lists only src/a.ts; other.txt is still staged (`git diff --cached --name-only` reads "other.txt") and notes.txt still untracked
2. given a repo where src/a.ts is committed with "export const a = 1;\n" and is unchanged; paths ["src/a.ts"]; when committed; then null; HEAD is the commit it was before

Data Commit Info: One commit and what it changed; structurally runloop's CommitInfo, so makeCommitHook is a CommitHook.
Schema:
{ commit: string, diffstat: { files: number, insertions: number, deletions: number } }

Module: `src/git/commit.ts`; test: `src/git/commit.ts`.

## Function Commit Card

Stages exactly the card's targets; subject 'morph <id>: <targets>'; trailers Morph-Card, Morph-Model, Morph-Variant (if given), Morph-Acceptance-Exit; returns sha and diffstat, or null when nothing changed. makeCommitHook binds it into runloop's commit hook.

Behaviour: commitCard(root, {customId, targets, model, variant, acceptanceExit}, env) is Commit Paths over targets with subject "morph <customId>: <targets joined by ", ">" and trailers Morph-Card <customId>, Morph-Model <model>, Morph-Variant <variant> only when variant is not null, Morph-Acceptance-Exit <acceptanceExit>, in that order. makeCommitHook(root, model, env) returns (customId, targets) => commitCard(root, {customId, targets, model, variant: null, acceptanceExit: 0}, env): runloop fires its hook only for an accepted card (exit 0) and does not pass the winning variant, so the hook writes no Morph-Variant.

Steps:
- calls: Commit Paths
- produces: Commit Info

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given a repo on morph/r1; src/a.ts written "export const a = 1;\n" (new) and src/b.ts written "export const b = 2;\nexport const c = 3;\n" (new); customId "a", targets ["src/a.ts", "src/b.ts"], model "glm53", variant null, acceptanceExit 0; when committed; then {commit: HEAD (40 hex), diffstat {files: 2, insertions: 3, deletions: 0}}; the HEAD message is "morph a: src/a.ts, src/b.ts\n\nMorph-Card: a\nMorph-Model: glm53\nMorph-Acceptance-Exit: 0"; `git log -1 --format=%(trailers:key=Morph-Card,valueonly)` reads "a"
2. given a repo where src/a.ts is committed with "export const a = 1;\n"; then src/a.ts rewritten "export const a = 2;\nexport const z = 0;\n"; customId "c", targets ["src/a.ts"], model "glm53", variant "c.v2", acceptanceExit 0; when committed; then diffstat {files: 1, insertions: 2, deletions: 1}; the HEAD message is "morph c: src/a.ts\n\nMorph-Card: c\nMorph-Model: glm53\nMorph-Variant: c.v2\nMorph-Acceptance-Exit: 0"
3. given a fresh repo; hook = makeCommitHook(root, "stub", env); out/h.ts written "x\n"; then the hook called again with nothing changed; when hook("h", ["out/h.ts"]), then hook("h", ["out/h.ts"]); then first {commit: HEAD, diffstat {files: 1, insertions: 1, deletions: 0}} with the HEAD message "morph h: out/h.ts\n\nMorph-Card: h\nMorph-Model: stub\nMorph-Acceptance-Exit: 0"; second null and HEAD unchanged

Data Commit Info: One commit and what it changed; structurally runloop's CommitInfo, so makeCommitHook is a CommitHook.
Schema:
{ commit: string, diffstat: { files: number, insertions: number, deletions: number } }

## Function Open Run Branch

morph/<runId> from HEAD; refuses a dirty tree outside .morph/ and an existing branch.

Behaviour: openRunBranch(root, runId, env): runId must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, else {ok: false, error: "invalid runId: <runId>"} and no git call. Then `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`: every entry's path (the text after the two status letters and a space; for a rename the path after " -> ") that does not start with ".morph/" is dirty; any dirty path → {ok: false, error: "dirty tree outside .morph/: <dirty paths sorted, joined by ", ">"}. Then base = `git rev-parse HEAD` (trimmed); a branch refs/heads/morph/<runId> that already exists → {ok: false, error: "branch morph/<runId> already exists"}; else `git checkout -q -b morph/<runId>` and {ok: true, branch: "morph/<runId>", base}. A refusal leaves the checkout and the refs as they were.

Steps:
- calls: Run Git
- produces: Branch Result

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given a fresh repo on main whose HEAD is <h>; runId "r1"; when opened; then {ok: true, branch: "morph/r1", base: <h>} (40 hex chars); `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` now reads "morph/r1"
2. given a fresh repo with the untracked files .morph/deck.json and .morph/runs/x/report.json; runId "r2"; when opened; then {ok: true, branch: "morph/r2", base: <h>} — files under .morph/ do not make the tree dirty
3. given a repo with README.md committed and then modified, and an untracked src/a.ts; runId "r3"; when opened; then {ok: false, error: "dirty tree outside .morph/: README.md, src/a.ts"}; the checkout is still main and no branch morph/r3 exists
4. given a fresh repo where the branch morph/r4 already exists (git branch morph/r4); runId "r4"; then runId "a b"; when opened; then {ok: false, error: "branch morph/r4 already exists"}, the checkout still main; then {ok: false, error: "invalid runId: a b"}

Data Branch Result: The run branch opened, or the refusal.
Schema:
{ ok: true, branch: string, base: string } | { ok: false, error: string }

## Function Archive Run

Writes .morph/runs/<runId>/{deck.json, report.json} and commits them with Morph-Run trailers; append-only.

Behaviour: archiveRun(root, {runId, deck, report}, env): runId must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, else {ok: false, error: "invalid runId: <runId>"}. dir = ".morph/runs/<runId>"; an existing root/dir → {ok: false, error: "archive <dir> already exists"}, nothing written (a run id names one run forever). Else mkdir -p, write <dir>/deck.json = JSON.stringify(deck.cards, null, 2) + "\n" (the Deck File form, a JSON array of cards) and <dir>/report.json = JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) + "\n", then Commit Paths over [<dir>/deck.json, <dir>/report.json] with subject "morph run <runId>: deck and report" and trailers Morph-Run <runId>, Morph-Cards <deck.cards.length>, Morph-Written, Morph-Failed, Morph-Skipped, Morph-Budget-Exceeded (the number of report.outcomes with that status). → {ok: true, dir, commit: the sha, or null when Commit Paths returned null}. A git failure of the commit (an ignored .morph/ makes git add refuse) → {ok: false, error: "archive <dir> written but not committed: <the Error's message>"}; the files stay on disk.

Steps:
- reads: Deck
- reads: Run Report
- calls: Commit Paths
- produces: Archive Result
